title: New Jersey AI Laws

reading.body:
New Jersey's only AI-related law targets rent-setting software, not AI development, and it was passed on 2026-07-20 as A3497, the Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act.

The pattern is narrow and sectoral. The law does not regulate AI as a technology. It amends the New Jersey Antitrust Act to reach a specific commercial practice: rental property owners using coordinators, coordinators facilitating agreements among owners that restrict competition, parallel pricing coordination by two or more persons, and performing a coordinating function at all. It defines algorithmic device, coordinating function, and competitively sensitive information, and it requires the Attorney General to establish a complaint location and authorizes rulemaking.

For AI specifically, this is a case where the binding constraint runs through software rather than through compute, buildings, or power. The law's subject is an algorithmic device used to set prices, and its enforcement mechanism is antitrust plus a complaint channel, not a data center, an interconnection queue, or a generation asset. Nothing in the enrolled text as summarized here touches siting, electricity procurement, or physical infrastructure.

What this does not tell the reader: it is one law, so it says nothing about New Jersey's broader posture, and it covers no other AI application. The data gives no effective date, no penalty amounts, no enforcement record, and no count of bills that failed or remain pending. It also does not establish whether the law has been tested in court.

New Jersey has enacted 1 AI-related law. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in New Jersey

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • A3497: Establishes "Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act." passed 2026-07-20

    The act makes it unlawful and a violation of the New Jersey Antitrust Act for rental property owners to use coordinators that perform coordinating functions, for coordinators to facilitate agreements among rental property owners that restrict competition, for two or more persons to engage in parallel pricing coordination, and for any person to perform a coordinating function. It defines key terms such as algorithmic device, coordinating function, and competitively sensitive information. It requires the Attorney General to establish a complaint location and authorizes rulemaking.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for New Jersey. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
